answer: History is time-locked, so a key cannot rewrite its own receipts after an audit. Failure is published with the key attached, and because the quorum has to come from unrelated networks a cluster of friendly reviewers reads as one mirror rather than five opinions. The effect is that a farm's first mistake stays attached to every key it ever touches. A vine grows on what it is given, and a pulse of bad work propagates along the same path the payout came from.
